items.title: Cyborg roaches to the rescue?
items.summary: Researchers have developed cyborg cockroaches that can survive underwater and in low-oxygen environments, allowing them to assist in search-and-rescue operations. The cockroaches are fitted with electronic controllers, an oxygen generation tank, and silicone tubes, enabling them to navigate for up to 3 hours. The cyborg insects were tested during Myanmar's 7.7-magnitude earthquake in March 2025, where they relayed information to identify signs of life.
items.audio_script: From thehustle.co, "Cyborg roaches to the rescue?" Researchers have developed cyborg cockroaches that can survive underwater and in low-oxygen environments, demonstrating a key result in search-and-rescue operations. The development of these cyborg insects involved the integration of electronic controllers, an oxygen generation tank, and silicone tubes, allowing them to navigate for up to 3 hours. The cyborg cockroaches were tested during Myanmar's 7.7-magnitude earthquake in March 2025, where they relayed information to identify signs of life. The success of these tests indicates that the cyborg roaches can potentially be used in future search-and-rescue operations, particularly in environments with limited accessibility.

items.title: Video Friday: Lift Happens
items.summary: DARPA Lift Challenge showcases robots learning to lift and maneuver objects safely. STEMbot, a small robot, climbs plant stems to check for pests. A new robot from Modlab University of Pennsylvania has a "truss't-worthy" design, and DR02 from DEEP Robotics navigates stairs with stable movement. Meanwhile, a miniature robotic structural minifridge has been developed.
items.audio_script: From IEEE Spectrum - Robotics, "Video Friday: Lift Happens", DARPA's Lift Challenge showcased robots learning to lift and maneuver objects safely, resulting in significant advancements in robotic dexterity and object handling capabilities. The challenge saw the development and deployment of various robotic systems, including STEMbot, a small robot that successfully climbed plant stems to check for pests, and a new robot from Modlab University of Pennsylvania, which boasted a "truss-worthy" design that enabled stable lifting and manipulation of objects. Meanwhile, DR02 from DEEP Robotics demonstrated stable movement on stairs, and a miniature robotic structural minifridge was also developed, showcasing the diversity of innovative robotic designs being explored in this field.
